message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Nightly

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - master
    paths:
      - "src/**"
      - "templates/userscript/**"
      - "build/**"
      - "package.json"
      - "package-lock.json"
      - ".github/workflows/nightly.yaml"
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: nightly
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  nightly:
    if: github.repository == 'adsbypasser/adsbypasser'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: "npm"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run tests
        run: npm test

      - name: Build userscripts
        run: npm run build
        env:
          ADSBYPASSER_NIGHTLY: "1"

      - name: Deploy to nightly repository
        run: ./build/ci/deploy-nightly.sh
        env:
          SOURCE_DIR: ./dist
          TARGET_REPO: ${{ vars.GH_NIGHTLY_REPO }}
          TARGET_REPO_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
          COMMIT_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
",
  "rationale": "The nightly job has no explicit timeout, so it falls back to the default 360-minute job limit and can consume a long runner window if a step hangs. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern (bound jobs with a custom timeout) is supported by the measured experiment example batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508, which added timeout-minutes: 5 to a job and retained all successes while reducing elapsed time. The change is minimal: only timeout-minutes: 5 is added to the job. All existing steps (checkout, Node setup with npm cache, install, tests, build, deploy) and the existing concurrency cancel-in-progress, path filters, and permissions are preserved, so build/test coverage and the deploy step are unchanged. No permissions are weakened, no new secrets or network access are added, and no publishing/deployment operation is introduced.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508", "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT"]
}
